title: De-AI Your UI: Pricing Page Optimization
summary: This lesson teaches how to optimize AI-generated pricing pages by establishing visual hierarchy, simplifying feature lists, and communicating value through currency-based savings rather than percentages.

transcript.text: Three identical tiers, a badge on each, 12 checkmarks. AI made, five tells.
Tell one: Only one tier gets the highlight. Three equal cards is no recommendation. The middle one lifts, the others step back. The top tier exists to make it feel fair.
Tell two: Most popular on one tier. A badge on every card is a badge on none. The rest get nothing, not a smaller badge. Silence is what makes the label work.
Tell three: List what changes between tiers, not 12 checkmarks that repeat. Everything in Starter, plus and three lines. 12 identical checks are a wall, not a comparison.
Tell four: One primary button on the page. Gradient buttons on all three is the AI signature. Filled on the picked, outlined on the rest. The eye lands on one click.
Tell five: Annual toggle with the saving written in money. $98 off beats 17% off. Nobody computes percent at checkout. The monthly price stays, struck through.

Five tells fixed. One tier that sells. Now make Claude Code think like a senior UX designer. UX Engine designs a screen before coding, audits what is broken, reviews the diff, and kills the AI look. Link in bio.
